title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Strengthening the Work of Court Forensic Medicine
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Strengthening Court Forensic Medical Work

Fa (Si) Fa [1986] No. 34

To all local people's courts at various levels nationwide:

Pursuant to the provision of the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China that "local people's courts at all levels shall have forensic medical personnel," in recent years, with the active efforts of people's courts at all levels, the forensic medical work of the people's courts has seen considerable development. Up to now, 28 High People's Courts, 198 Intermediate People's Courts, and 570 Basic People's Courts have been equipped with forensic medical technicians, totaling 1,032 persons. Some High and Intermediate People's Courts have successively established and improved forensic medical institutions, carrying out forensic technical work such as examinations, reviews, and expert evaluations, thereby providing scientific evidence for judicial officers in correctly convicting and sentencing, and in resolving civil and economic dispute cases, and playing an important role in avoiding miscarriages of justice, false cases, and wrong cases, and ensuring the quality of case handling. However, at present, the forensic medical work of the people's courts is still a weak link, with a serious shortage of forensic medical technicians, underdeveloped forensic medical institutions, and primitive working conditions, far from meeting the needs of trial work. This should draw sufficient attention from leading comrades of courts at all levels. In order to strengthen the forensic medical work of the people's courts and fully utilize the role of forensic science in trial work, we hereby notify the relevant issues as follows:

1. Main Tasks and Scope of Duties of Forensic Medical Technical Work

The main task of forensic medical technical work in the courts is to use modern science and technology to accurately and promptly ascertain and determine the true circumstances of a case, provide scientific evidence for trial work, protect the legitimate rights and interests of the state, collectives, and citizens, and ensure the correct implementation of state laws.

The main duties of forensic medical technical work in the courts are to examine and evaluate the following items submitted by entrusting units:

(1) Conduct examinations and evaluations of living persons (human bodies) in criminal and civil cases, including injuries, mental states, physiological conditions, paternity testing, etc.

(2) Examine, evaluate, and photograph the corpses of executed criminals. Conduct review evaluations of corpses where the cause of death is unclear and further dissection is needed.

(3) Examine, evaluate, and conduct review evaluations of relevant physical evidence, documentary evidence, poisons, and traces in case files.

(4) Examine and evaluate other forensic medicine-related materials in cases accepted by the people's courts.

2. Forensic Medical Institutions and Staffing

Establishing and improving forensic medical institutions is the key to doing a good job in forensic medical technical work. Each High and Intermediate People's Court shall establish a Forensic Medical Technical Office (which should be at the same level as the court's divisions and offices). Basic People's Courts shall be equipped with full-time forensic medical technicians. Specific requirements are as follows:

(1) High People's Courts that have already established Forensic Medical Technical Offices shall actively carry out various professional work, and gradually establish sub-offices for physical evidence, pathology, living body examination, and toxicological analysis as needed and where possible. Those that have not yet established institutions or assigned personnel shall actively select and transfer forensic medical technicians and establish Forensic Medical Technical Offices.

The Forensic Medical Technical Office of a High People's Court shall be staffed with 8 to 12 persons.

(2) Intermediate People's Courts that have already established Forensic Medical Technical Offices shall gradually carry out work such as living body examinations, physical and documentary evidence examinations, and corpse dissections. Those that have not yet established institutions shall strive to create conditions and gradually establish Forensic Medical Technical Offices.

The Forensic Medical Technical Office of an Intermediate People's Court shall be staffed with 4 to 8 persons.

(3) Basic People's Courts that do not yet have forensic medical technicians shall gradually be equipped with 1 to 3 forensic medical technicians. Where work requires and conditions permit, a Forensic Medical Technical Office may be established.

3. Technical Titles of Forensic Medical Technicians

Pursuant to the reply of the Central Leading Group for Title Reform Work on the "Request for Forensic Medical Technicians to Use the Health Technical Title Series" (Gai Zi Gai Zi [1986] No. 47), it is stipulated that "in the implementation of the professional technical title appointment work, in accordance with the 'Interim Regulations on Health Technical Titles' and the characteristics of forensic medical work, the title names for forensic medical technicians shall be correspondingly set as: Chief Forensic Physician, Deputy Chief Forensic Physician, Senior Forensic Physician, Forensic Physician, and Assistant Forensic Physician." Specific evaluation methods shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of the "Detailed Implementation Rules for Forensic Medical Technicians Using the 'Interim Regulations on Health Technical Personnel Titles'" jointly issued by the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Justice (Gong Fa [1986] No. 15). Currently, preparations for title evaluation should be promptly carried out.

5. Training of Forensic Medical Technicians

During the Seventh Five-Year Plan period, training of existing forensic medical technicians shall be emphasized. By 1990, through training, 50% of the 400 forensic medical technicians with a secondary specialized education level shall reach a college level. Forensic physicians who have a medical education level of college or above but have not received specialized forensic medical training shall all undergo rotational training once before 1990.

6. Strengthening Technical Equipment

Technical equipment and workrooms for forensic medical work are necessary conditions for conducting forensic technical evaluations. People's courts at all levels shall purchase forensic medical equipment according to the actual needs of forensic medical technical work, and shall promptly resolve the issue of workrooms for forensic medical work.

The Supreme People's Court plans to establish a Forensic Technical Evaluation Center for the court system in the future, based on the forensic medical technical offices of courts with strong technical capabilities, relatively complete equipment, and well-developed forensic medical technical work, to serve the judicial evaluation work of the national court system.

The above notice is to be earnestly implemented. If there are any problems or opinions during implementation, please promptly report to our court.

December 31, 1986
